result:
March billing adjustments for US are complete. Summary of what I did:

**Tested every item against contracts + the final March usage and uptime reports before booking anything.**

**Booked (2):**
- **JE-00304** — Acme Logistics March usage overage, **$1,136.00**. 1,284,000 calls − 1,000,000 included = 284,000 × $0.004 per Order Form 3. Posted Dr 1300 Unbilled Receivables / Cr 4100 Usage Revenue (invoice not yet issued, so unbilled per policy §6, unlike Jan/Feb which had invoices). Support: DOC-0003, DOC-0210.
- **JE-00305** — Beacon Health SLA credit, **$800.00**. us-west uptime 99.31% < 99.5% threshold (incident INC-2291), credit = 10% × $8,000. Posted Dr 4000 Subscription Revenue / Cr 1100 AR as a revenue reduction per policy §7. Support: DOC-0002, DOC-0211.

**Not booked / flagged (EXC-001):**
- **Corvid Retail's $2,500 credit request — declined.** Their region (us-central) ran 99.94%, above the 99.5% SLA threshold; the March outage was in us-west and didn't touch them, and their contract says "no other credits apply." The requested amount also exceeds the contractual maximum ($1,150) even if an SLA miss had occurred. Flagged for controller rather than accommodated.

**Also confirmed no overage was due from Beacon, Corvid, Fairview or Evergreen** (no usage terms and/or under the included threshold), and no other customer missed SLA.

Two follow-ups worth your attention: Beacon already paid INV-2112 in full, so the $800 sits as a credit balance in AR to apply in April — billing needs the credit memo raised; and there's **no master agreement on file for Fairview Labs or Evergreen Bank**, which didn't matter this month but leaves future usage/SLA terms untestable.
